findings.title: [P2] Fail explicitly when a captured review could not run
findings.body: When a review has zero confidence because execution was blocked, this condition silently skips it and allows the sync to succeed, exactly as if there were no review to publish. It also swallows malformed-JSON errors from jq. Distinguish absent reviews from failed checks and parsing failures, and return a failure for the latter cases rather than reporting successful synchronization. This follows **A broken instrument fails the run. A refuted hypothesis is a result.** ([AGENTS.md:25–29](AGENTS.md#L25-L29)).

findings.title: [P2] Associate the posted review with the reviewed commit
findings.body: If the branch advances between the review and synchronization, omitting `commit_id` makes GitHub attach this review to the latest PR head, although the verdict describes an earlier revision. Read the recorded commit and either supply it as `commit_id` or verify that it still matches the PR head before publishing, so an older clean verdict is not presented as a review of newer changes.

review.overall_explanation: The sync hides failed review execution and can attach stale verdicts to newer PR revisions. Both undermine the reliability of the published review results.
